title: Redis Client
concept: Redis client for XIOM — connect to Redis servers for caching, message queues, pub/sub, and real-time data structures.
why: Redis is the most popular in-memory data store. From caching to rate limiting to real-time analytics, Redis powers the data layer of modern applications.
tips: Use SETEX for cache entries with TTL — automatic cleanup prevents memory leaks
Sorted sets are perfect for leaderboards, priority queues, and time-series data
Connection pooling is essential for web servers — one connection per request is too slow
Use Redis pipelining for batch operations — reduces round-trips dramatically
common_mistakes: Not setting TTL on cache entries — Redis memory grows unbounded
Using KEYS command in production — it blocks Redis. Use SCAN instead
Forgetting that Redis is single-threaded — expensive operations block all other commands
